bundles.evidenceText: in a universe without a God in it the same thing applies
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts that the same arithmetic relation holds in universes with and without God. That proposition directly supports the subsidiary logic bridge claiming logical and mathematical relations hold independently of any deity. The central natural-order bridge is excluded because the assertion concerns arithmetic, not observed complexity or natural processes.

bundles.evidenceText: religious reasons to justify the evil that they know that they're doing
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts that people already recognize conduct as evil while using religious doctrine to rationalize it. This attacks the subsidiary morality bridge's claim that objective obligations require a transcendent lawgiver, because moral recognition is presented as prior to and potentially corrupted by dogma. The motion bridge is excluded because no complete creator explanation is addressed.

bundles.evidenceText: there has to be something that gets this whole thing going
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts that something must originate the universe and distinguishes that origin from Darwinian processes concerning things inside space and time. This directly supports the central origin bridge requiring an originating cause beyond processes operating within space and time. The motion bridge is excluded because the excerpt does not defend a mind-like ground for every listed domain.

bundles.evidenceText: you have to have room for a god like that to have reasons that you don't know about
bundles.rationale: The excerpt asserts only that a sufficiently great God may have reasons unknown to human critics. No route contact exists because this epistemic possibility neither supports nor attacks any stated origin, logic, or morality bridge, so no bridge or polarity is selected. The motion bridge is the nearest competitor but is excluded because unknown divine reasons do not establish that a mind-like creator best explains the complete motion-level set of phenomena.
